[[Malta]] competed at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in [[London]], which was held from 27 July to 12 August 2012. The country's participation at London marked its fifteenth appearance in the Summer Olympics since its début at the [[1928 Summer Olympics]]. The delegation included two track and field athletes, [[Rachid Chouhal]] and [[Diane Borg]], one double trap shooter [[William Chetcuti]] and two swimmers [[Andrew Chetcuti]] and [[Nicola Muscat]]. All five competitors qualified for the Games through [[Wild card (sports)|wildcard]] places. William Chetcuti was selected as the flag bearer for the [[2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]] while Borg held it at the [[2012 Summer Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]]. Choudai did not progress beyond the preliminary stages of the men's [[Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|100 metres]], while Borg advanced to the first round of the women's [[Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metres|100 metres]] before being eliminated. William Chetcuti finished ninth in the [[Shooting at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's double trap|double trap shooting]] event, while Andrew Chetcuti and Muscat were unable to progress to the first rounds of their respective swimming disciplines.

==Background==
Malta participated in fifteen Olympic Games between its début at the [[1928 Summer Olympics]] in [[Amsterdam]], Netherlands and the 2012 Summer Olympics in London, England,<ref name=maltaolympichistory>{{cite web|title=Countries – Malta |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/MLT/ |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161014144300/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/MLT/ |archive-date=14 October 2016 }}</ref> with the exception of 1932, 1952, 1956, 1964 and 1976.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9mM0XzW03AcC&q=Malta&pg=PR69 |title=Historical Dictionary of the d Olympic Movement |last1=Mallon |first1=Bill|author-link=Bill Mallon|last2=Heijmans |first2=Jeroen |publisher=[[Rowman & Littlefield|Scarecrow Press]] |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-8108-7522-7 |page=213 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107170018/https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=9mM0XzW03AcC&pg=PR69&redir_esc=y |archive-date= 7 November 2016 }}</ref> No Maltese athlete has ever won a medal at the Olympic Games.<ref name=maltaolympichistory/> Malta participated in the Summer Olympics from 27 July to 12 August 2012.<ref name=malta2012>{{cite web|title=Malta at the 2012 London Summer Games |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/MLT/summer/2012/ |publisher=Sports Reference |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161203141029/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/MLT/summer/2012/ |archive-date= 3 December 2016 }}</ref> Malta sent sprinters [[Rachid Chouhal]] and [[Diane Borg]], shooter [[William Chetcuti]] and swimmers [[Andrew Chetcuti]] and [[Nicola Muscat]] to London.<ref name="malta2012" /> As in the [[2004 Summer Olympics]], Chetcuti was the flag bearer for the opening ceremony while Borg held it for the closing ceremony.<ref name="malta-fb">{{cite news|author=Staff |date=20 July 2012 |title=Chetcuti to carry Malta's flag |url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20120720/sport/Chetcuti-to-carry-Malta-s-flag.429348 |access-date=20 July 2012 |work=[[Times of Malta]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220080653/http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20120720/sport/Chetcuti-to-carry-Malta-s-flag.429348 |archive-date=20 December 2013 }}</ref><ref name="Flagbearers closing">{{cite web|url=http://www.olympic.org/Documents/Games_London_2012/London_2012_Closing_Ceremony-Flag_Bearers.pdf|title=London 2012 Closing Ceremony – Flag Bearers|publisher=Olympic.org.|access-date=7 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815055250/https://stillmed.olympic.org/Documents/Games_London_2012/London_2012_Closing_Ceremony-Flag_Bearers.pdf|archive-date=15 August 2016}}</ref> Along with the five athletes, the Malta Olympic team consisted of chef de mission and the country's NOC vice-president Julian Pace Bonello, director of sport and assistant Mark Cutajar, secretary general Joe Cassar and director of finance David Azzopardi.<ref name="maltadelegation">{{cite news|title=London 2012 Olympics: Maltese Contingent leaves for London this morning |url=http://www.independent.com.mt/articles/2012-07-26/others/london-2012-olympics-maltese-contingent-leaves-for-london-this-morning-313725/ |work=[[The Malta Independent]] |date=26 July 2012 |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107161403/http://www.independent.com.mt/articles/2012-07-26/others/london-2012-olympics-maltese-contingent-leaves-for-london-this-morning-313725/ |archive-date= 7 November 2016 }}</ref> The athletes were coached by Jimmy Bugeja, Andy Colbourn and Mario Bonello, with Lucienne Attard, Adele Muscat and Milos Stanisavljevic from the Maltese NOC's medical commission attending the Games.<ref name="maltadelegation" />

==Athletics==
{{main|Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics}}
[[File:Diane Borg 2012.jpg|thumb|[[Diane Borg]] competing in the women's 100 metres where she was eliminated from the event's first round.]]
Rachid Chouhal was the oldest athlete to represent Malta at the London Games at the age of 37. He had not participated in any previous Olympic Games.<ref name="malta2012" /> Chouhal qualified for the Games via a wildcard because his fastest time of 10.83 seconds, set at the Marsa Sports Complex on 2 June 2012, was 0.59 seconds slower than the "B" qualifying standard for his event, the men's [[Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|100 metres]].<ref name="Athletics qualification">{{cite web|date=15 April 2011|title=London 2012 Olympics: Athletics qualification|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/8453553/London-2012-Olympics-Athletics-qualification.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111002225133/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/8453553/London-2012-Olympics-Athletics-qualification.html|archive-date=2 October 2011|access-date=5 March 2015|website=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iaaf.org/athletes/malta/rachid-chouhal-172225 |title=Rachid Chouhal – Athlete Profile – Progression |publisher=[[International Association of Athletics Federations|IAAF]] |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107162854/https://www.iaaf.org/athletes/malta/rachid-chouhal-172225 |archive-date= 7 November 2016 }}</ref> Before the Games Choudal said "When I want something, I go for it. I am not afraid. I am confident in my training and am careful not to get hurt. I know that the level of the athletes competing in the 100 metre sprint is very high. My aim is to do a personal best or season's best."<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20120725/sport/let-the-games-begin-july-25-2012.430083 |title=Let the games begin – July 25, 2012 |last=Facchetti |first=Josianne |date=25 July 2012 |work=The Times of Malta |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202001054/http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20120725/sport/let-the-games-begin-july-25-2012.430083 |archive-date= 2 February 2017 }}</ref> He was drawn in the fourth heat of the preliminary round on 4 August, finishing fourth out of eight runners, with a time of 10.83 seconds.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/olympics/summer/2012/results/_/event/256/discipline/3 |title=2012 Summer Olympics – Results – Athletics – Men's 100m |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021072105/http://www.espn.co.uk/olympics/summer/2012/results/_/event/256/discipline/3 |archive-date=21 October 2016 }}</ref> Overall Chouhal finished 58th out of 75 athletes, but did not progress to the first round because he was 0.21 seconds slower than the slowest competitor in his heat who went through to the later stages.<ref name=":1" />

Competing at her first Olympic Games at the age of 21, Diane Borg carried the flag of Malta at the closing ceremony.<ref name="Flagbearers closing" /> She qualified for the London Games as a wildcard entrant, because her fastest time of 11.89 seconds, set at the [[2011 Games of the Small States of Europe]], was 0.51 seconds slower than the "B" qualifying standard for the women's [[Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metres|100 metres]].<ref name="Athletics qualification" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iaaf.org/athletes/malta/diane-borg-208963 |title=Diane Borg – Athlete Profile – Progression |publisher=IAAF |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107163028/https://www.iaaf.org/athletes/malta/diane-borg-208963 |archive-date= 7 November 2016 }}</ref> She stated that it was "a great feeling" that she would be representing Malta and every person hoping that she would perform well.<ref name=":0" /> Borg took part in the event's second heat on 3 August, finishing third out of eight entrants, with a time of 12 seconds. Her finishing position allowed her to advance to the first round as the slowest qualifier.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://london2012.nytimes.com/track-and-field/womens-100m |title=Track and Field / Womenʼs 100m |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160709115810/http://london2012.nytimes.com/track-and-field/womens-100m |archive-date= 9 July 2016 }}</ref> Borg was drawn in the second heat of the first round, held on the same day, placing eighth (and last) of all competitors, with a time of 11.92 seconds. She finished 53rd out of 78 runners overall,{{#tag:ref|One athlete, [[Noor Al-Malki|Noor Hussain Al-Malki]], did not finish.<ref name=":2"/>|group="n"}}  and was unable to advance to the semi-finals because her time was 0.57 seconds slower than the slowest athlete who progressed to the next stage.<ref name=":2" />

==Shooting==
{{main|Shooting at the 2012 Summer Olympics}}
[[File:London-Woolwich, Barrack Field & Royal Artillery Barracks.jpg|thumb|The [[Royal Artillery Barracks]], where William Chetcuti competed in the men's double trap shooting competition.]]William Checuti was the only member of the Maltese team at the London Olympics to have participated in three previous Olympic Games and was his country's sole representative in the men's [[Shooting at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's double trap|double trap shooting]] competition.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-294026845.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180517153532/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-294026845.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 May 2018|title=Olympic Solidarity: William Chetcuti|date=21 June 2012|work=States News Service|access-date=7 November 2016}}</ref> He qualified for the event by receiving a wildcard from the Tripartite Commission because of his performance at the [[2011 ISSF World Cup|2011 ISSF Shotgun World Cup]] where he achieved a gold medal.<ref name=":3" /> William Chetcuti said that his objective was "to do his best" and in the event he performed well, he felt that he would be at an equivalent level to his rival competitors.<ref name=":0" /> On 2 August he competed in the qualification round of the men's double trap. He finished ninth out of 23 athletes,{{#tag:ref|One shooter, [[Sergio Piñero]], was unable to finish.<ref name=shootingresults/>|group="n"}} with a score of 135 points. William Chetcuti scored eight points less than the highest scoring competitor [[Peter Wilson (sport shooter)|Peter Wilson]] of [[Great Britain at the 2012 Summer Olympics|Great Britain]]. He scored two points less than [[Sweden at the 2012 Summer Olympics|Sweden]]'s [[Håkan Dahlby]] and [[Richárd Bognár]] from [[Hungary at the 2012 Summer Olympics|Hungary]] who were the lowest scoring qualifiers for the final and therefore his competition ended at the qualifying round.<ref name=shootingresults>{{Cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/london-2012/shooting/double-trap-150-targets-men |title=London 2012 / Shooting – Double Trap 150 Targets Men |publisher=Olympic.org |access-date=7 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107155525/https://www.olympic.org/london-2012/shooting/double-trap-150-targets-men |archive-date= 7 November 2016 }}</ref> After the Games William Chetcuti said he gave it his best but on the day he did not perform to the best of his ability. He stated that his result was influenced by missing his targets in the first and third rounds.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportinmalta.com/william-chetcuti-misses-olympic-final-for-2-clays/ |title=William Chetcuti |date=2 August 2012 |website=Sport in Malta |access-date=7 November 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107160153/http://www.sportinmalta.com/william-chetcuti-misses-olympic-final-for-2-clays/ |archive-date=7 November 2016 }}</ref>

==Swimming==
{{main|Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics}}
[[File:London Aquatics Centre, 16 April 2012.jpg|thumb|The [[London Aquatics Centre]], where Andrew Checuti and Muscat competed in swimming events.]]The 2012 London Summer Games marked Andrew Checuti's début in the quadrennial competition. He was the youngest male athlete on the national team, at age 19.<ref name="malta2012" /> Andrew Chetcuti qualified for the Games after being issued with a universality place from swimming's world governing body [[FINA]] after his fastest time of 51.98 seconds, set at the 2011 Games of the Small States of Europe, was 0.95 seconds slower "B" qualifying standard for his event, the men's [[Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metre freestyle|100 metre freestyle]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|url=https://swimswam.com/fina-announces-qualifying-standards-for-london-2012/|title=FINA Announces Qualifying Standards for London 2012|last=Keith|first=Branden|date=25 November 2010|website=Swim Swam|access-date=17 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161020001240/https://swimswam.com/fina-announces-qualifying-standards-for-london-2012/|archive-date=20 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://gulfnews.com/sport/more-sport/primary-school-dream-to-olympic-reality-1.1038813 |title=Primary school dream to Olympic reality |last=Hammond |first=Ashley |date=22 June 2012 |work=[[Gulf News]] |access-date=7 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108052055/http://gulfnews.com/sport/more-sport/primary-school-dream-to-olympic-reality-1.1038813 |archive-date= 8 November 2016 }}</ref> He spent time in Dubai and South Africa preparing for the Games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thenational.ae/sport/other-sport/hard-work-in-the-uae-pays-off-for-maltese-swimmer#full |title=Hard work in the UAE pays off for Maltese swimmer |last=Passela |first=Amith |date=14 June 2012 |work=[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National]] |access-date=7 November 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107162134/http://www.thenational.ae/sport/other-sport/hard-work-in-the-uae-pays-off-for-maltese-swimmer |archive-date= 7 November 2016 }}</ref> Andrew Chetcuti said it would be "the best experience of my life so far" and that he would attempt to enjoy competing in the Games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://link.galegroup.com/apps/doc/A297202342/GPS?sid=wikipedia|title=Glad to be going: Andrew Chetcuti will represent Malta at the Olympic Games in London. The Georgia Tech swimmer is eager to soak the experience all in|last=Hummer|first=Steve|date=7 November 2011|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|access-date=7 November 2016|via=General OneFile}}</ref> The swimmer revealed that he would attempt to record a new [[Athletics abbreviations#Bests|personal best]] time.<ref name=":0" /> He participated in the third heat on 31 July, finishing third out of eight swimmers, with a time of 51.67 seconds.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/olympics/summer/2012/results/_/event/320/discipline/39 |title=2012 Summer Olympics – Results – Swimming – Men's 100m Freestyle |website=ESPN |access-date=7 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107161220/http://www.espn.co.uk/olympics/summer/2012/results/_/event/320/discipline/39 |archive-date= 7 November 2016 }}</ref> Andrew Chetcuti's time was a new [[List of Maltese records in swimming|Maltese national record]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite news|url=http://gulfnews.com/sport/more-sport/chetcuti-sets-new-maltese-record-in-100m-freestyle-1.1055746 |title=Chetcuti sets new Maltese record in 100m freestyle |last=Hammond |first=Ashley |date=31 July 2012 |work=Gulf News |access-date=7 November 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108052211/http://gulfnews.com/sport/more-sport/chetcuti-sets-new-maltese-record-in-100m-freestyle-1.1055746 |archive-date= 8 November 2016 }}</ref> He finished 39th out of 56 competitors overall,{{#tag:ref|Four swimmers did not start.<ref name=":4"/>|group="n"}} and was unable to advance beyond the first round because he was 2.68 seconds slower than the slowest athlete who progressed to the later stages.<ref name=":4" /> After the event Andrew Chetcuti said he was happy with the achievement but hoped to go faster.<ref name=":5" />

Nicola Muscat was the youngest person to compete for Malta at the London Games at the age of 18. She had not taken part in any previous Olympic Games.<ref name="malta2012" /> Muscat qualified for the Games after receiving a wildcard from FINA because her fastest time of 26.87 seconds was 1.11 second slower than the "B" qualifying standard for her event, the women's [[Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle|50 metre freestyle]].<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":6">{{cite web|url=http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/events/london2012/sw/universality_places.pdf|title=FINA Universality Places|date=6 July 2012|publisher=[[FINA]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120711000550/http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/events/london2012/sw/universality_places.pdf|archive-date=11 July 2012|access-date=6 July 2012}}</ref> Before the Games she said, "Competing at international competitions makes you learn to be realistic about winning and making achievable aims. For example, my main aim at the Olympics is to break my own national record."<ref name=":0" /> Muscat was drawn in the event's fifth heat on 3 August, finishing fourth out of eight athletes, with a time of 27.22 seconds. Overall she ranked 43rd out of 73 swimmers,{{#tag:ref|One competitor, [[Eszter Dara]], did not start.<ref name=":8"/>|group="n"}} and was unable to advance to the semi-finals after finishing 1.94 seconds slower than the slowest competitor who made the later stages.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|title=Swimming / Womenʼs 50m Freestyle|url=http://london2012.nytimes.com/swimming/womens-50m-freestyle#heats|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412132202/http://london2012.nytimes.com/swimming/womens-50m-freestyle|archive-date=12 April 2016|access-date=7 November 2016|website=The New York Times}}</ref>
